newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambican central bank denies forex clampdown.
newsitem.headline: Mozambican central bank denies forex clampdown.

text.p: Mozambique's central bank on Wednesday denied a press report that citizens with foreign exchange accounts in Mozambican banks would soon be obliged to withdraw their money only in local currency.

The allegation, published in Tuesday's edition of the independent Maputo daily Mediafax, caused alarm among the many Mozambicans who bank payments in hard currency earned from foreign employers or through trade.
Mediafax said the new foreign exchange regulation had been sent to state and private banks and would come into force soon when published in the government gazette, the Boletim da Republica.

But the newspaper published a reply on Wednesday from the central bank (Banco de Mocambique) saying the regulation "contains no clause imposing any compulsory conversion of foreign exchange accounts in the national banking system".
The bank added: "There is no implication that the holders of forex accounts will be obliged to convert their holdings into meticais (the national currency) when making withdrawals."
A leading private banker in Maputo told Reuters he had read the new regulation and could see nothing in it that would force foreign exchange account holders to accept meticais when withdrawing cash.
U.S. dollars are the preferred currency in Mozambique where retailers and service providers offer a better rate of exchange than commercial banks.
Mozambicans also use foreign exchange to buy visas to visit neighbouring South Africa.
